types.instant: ISO-8601 whole-second timestamp with explicit Z or numeric offset; compare/output in UTC
types.money: nonnegative finite decimal string with exactly two fraction digits
types.fraction: nonnegative finite decimal string; not an implicit percent
types.positive-int: JSON integer greater than zero, excluding booleans
types.nonnegative-int: JSON integer at least zero, excluding booleans
types.currency: explicit currency code; no automatic conversion

rules: All example formulas, thresholds, cutoffs, caps, capacities and tie-breaks are fictional sample policy, not general standards.
Malformed row schemas reject the complete bundle with outputs {} and explicit issues; never silently drop malformed rows.
Duplicate primary row IDs reject the bundle; ambiguous highest business revisions quarantine the affected entity without arbitrary tie-breaking.
Eligible evidence has recorded_at <= as_of; later evidence is not used to decide the frozen snapshot.
Money uses Decimal and ROUND_HALF_UP at the documented per-line boundary; totals sum rounded values.
All date ranges and planning intervals are half-open unless explicitly documented otherwise.
Uncomputable expected amounts remain uncomputed, not zero; complete totals cannot be compared against partial expected amounts.
All business entities must have an explicit terminal review disposition.
Goldens are independently authored before baseline execution and never regenerated from baseline results.

native_required_facilities: approved native attachment and media inspection
already-available permitted bundled-stdlib execution when needed by generated output
execution.missing_capability_policy: Stop and report the native limitation; no runtime installer, service, scheduler, browser runner, or infrastructure workaround.

contradictory evidence and ambiguity with no arbitrary winner
date, cutoff, threshold and rounding boundaries
zero, one and multiple entities and variable loop counts
input-order invariance and stable output array ordering
strict malformed, deep, duplicate-key and nonfinite JSON through shared CLI
existing output and trace destinations are not overwritten

sources.title: Recording Proof of Delivery
sources.scope: JD Edwards EnterpriseOne Transportation Management 9.2 delivery confirmation
supported_claims: The POD form records delivery date, delivery time, and received-by information.
sources.limitations: Does not define our revision resolution, delivered-unit controls, required evidence policy, tariff or charge formula.

sources.title: Understanding Invoice Matching
sources.scope: JD Edwards EnterpriseOne Transportation Management 9.2 freight invoice matching
supported_claims: Freight invoice matching compares the invoice amount with calculated shipment charges.
The documented process then creates an accounts-payable voucher; this downstream action is outside the mock review.
sources.limitations: No universal tolerance, pricing, audit algorithm, automatic-payment permission, or Oracle-compatible import schema is claimed.

sources.title: Matching Freight Invoices
sources.scope: JD Edwards EnterpriseOne Transportation Management 9.2 invoice header and freight selection
supported_claims: Invoice header information includes supplier, invoice number and dates.
Selected freight charges are associated with the invoice for review.
sources.limitations: The baseline does not perform the documented voucher action or reproduce a live application schema.

sources.title: Work orders overview
supported_claims: A work order specifies a task and the labor, materials, services, and tools required for it.
sources.limitations: Does not validate actual equipment condition, readiness, isolation or authorization, and does not prescribe a scheduling method.

sources.title: Scheduling work based on resource availability
sources.scope: Maximo Manage Graphical Scheduling resource-availability review
supported_claims: Scheduling considers start/end requirements and craft, asset, location, item and tool availability.
The documented planning workflow includes checking resource availability and adjusting the schedule.
sources.limitations: Our grid, greedy search, resource capacities, priorities and contingent dependency rules are sample policy, not a Maximo optimizer or safe-to-work clearance.

sources.title: Resource planning in schedules
sources.scope: Maximo Manage resource requirements, craft hours and other resource availability
supported_claims: The resource view distinguishes required and available craft hours.
Other-resource availability includes assets, locations, items and tools, with calendar context for assets and locations.
sources.limitations: Calendar availability is not a legal, physical or safety authorization. No industry-wide staffing, work-window or overtime standard is inferred.

sources.title: Approvals overview
sources.scope: Project Operations Integrated with ERP and Project Operations Core approvals
supported_claims: Time, expense and material submissions have approval records.
Approved project entries create actuals; approval cancellation and recall can reverse those transactions.
sources.limitations: No approval, rejection, cancellation or recall is executed. Synthetic status fields are not a Microsoft API or supported direct-edit instruction.

sources.title: Proforma invoices
sources.scope: Project Operations Integrated with ERP proforma invoicing
supported_claims: Proforma review provides another level of approval before customer invoicing.
Ready-to-Invoice contract transactions can include approved time and expenses, and draft invoice details can be reviewed and adjusted.
sources.limitations: The mock does not implement native draft creation, automated invoice runs, milestones, tax, confirmation or ERP integration. Prices, receipt policies and caps are invented.

sources.title: Confirm a proforma project-based invoice
sources.scope: Project Operations Integrated with ERP proforma confirmation
supported_claims: Confirmation makes a project invoice read-only.
Confirmation creates financial actuals, including billed sales and relevant reversals.
sources.limitations: This source supports excluding confirmation and financial posting from the scenario, not any authority to perform them.

candidates.title: Delivery, POD and carrier charge reconciliation exception review
candidates.trigger: Day-close arrival of synthetic shipment, POD, carrier invoice, rate and review-history exports.
candidates.start: Freeze the supplied batch and cutoff, then inventory all six logical exports.
candidates.end: Produce complete shipment and invoice review artifacts, owned exceptions and proposed case closures/reopens.
candidates.boundary: No delivery confirmation, carrier contact, live TMS update, payment, voucher, financial approval or dispute submission. Ready-for-review is not approved-for-payment.
joins: Invoice line -> invoice by invoice_id and shipment by shipment_id; carriers/currencies must agree.
POD -> shipment by shipment_id; unique highest eligible revision only.
Rate -> carrier_id + lane_id + currency + planned-delivery UTC date in [valid_from, valid_to); exactly one match.
Prior case -> shipment_id + issue_code; re-evaluate against current evidence without editing the historical export.

rules.description: Use delivery date/time and received-by information as context for POD evidence review; strict completeness/revision requirements remain sample policy.
Compare invoice charges with shipment charge expectations and preserve invoice header associations; stop before voucher/payment.
Select unique highest revision recorded by cutoff; conflicting highest revisions, void POD, quantity mismatch or missing POD hold shipment pricing.
Exactly one rate must cover planned-delivery UTC date; overlapping or missing rates are held without arbitrary selection.
Fuel is linehaul times fraction rounded to cents; detention is ceil(excess gate seconds / block seconds) times block charge, capped, with zero excess giving zero blocks.
Absolute variance <= max(absolute tolerance, rounded expected times relative tolerance) is ready for human review; both signs outside tolerance are held.
Header total must equal line sum; duplicate shipment/charge billings and carrier/currency mismatches are explicit holds, not deduplicated.
Missing POD is overdue only strictly beyond configured grace. Re-evaluate prior issues and propose closed/still-open/reopened states.
Separate computed/uncomputed shipments and totals; never treat unknown expected amounts as zero or compare partial expected with full billed totals.

steps.trace: Selected revision/rate IDs, future/ambiguous exclusions.

steps.procedure: Compute actual dwell, excess, blocks, fuel, detention and expected amounts for priceable rows.
steps.trace: Real linehaul, dwell, block and expected intermediates.

steps.procedure: Compare billed amounts and integrity constraints; classify ready versus held.
steps.trace: Expected, billed, tolerance and branch for selected rows.

steps.procedure: Create evidence, ambiguity, duplication and variance review items with owners.
steps.trace: Actual issue IDs, amounts and age/next-action facts.

steps.trace: Prior/current case decisions from real joins.

steps.trace: Final ready/held/uncomputed counts and computable monetary totals.

output_design: Shipment reconciliation rows with selected evidence IDs, charge components, billed/expected/variance/tolerance and review disposition.
Invoice rollups with total billed, computable billed/expected, completeness flag and ready/held line amounts.
Owned exception queue with missing-POD age and next action.
Proposed prior-case closures/reopens and a complete batch accounting summary.

numeric_semantics.money_rounding: ROUND_HALF_UP per fuel calculation, then exact cent sums
numeric_semantics.duration: Use exact integer gate seconds; ceiling division occurs after subtracting free minutes, not after rounding dwell.

cases.design: Four shipments, two invoices, two previous cases. Rates use 10% fuel, 60 free minutes, 30-minute blocks at 25.00 capped at 100.00. Invoice D1 groups D01/D02; D2 groups D03/D04.
cases.derivation: D01: 1000+100+25=1125 and +5 equals tolerance. D02: excess 70 minutes rounds up to three blocks, 800+80+75=955. D04 has no excess, 400+40=440. D03 is 51 hours late with no eligible POD, so no expected amount is invented.

cases.design: Three different shipments/contracts, a 15-minute block policy and cap changes, UTC effective-date rollover, new eligible POD closing history and a future void revision. A01 planned local September 30 at 20:00-04:00 selects the October 1 UTC rate.
cases.derivation: A01's 10.325 relative allowance rounds half-up to 10.33, exactly the variance. A02's excess 76 minutes requires six 15-minute blocks; 120.00 is capped at 60.00. A03 uses eligible revision 2, not future void revision 3.

cases.design: Four new shipments; only-future POD, two active rates, undercharge, and exact free-wait boundary. Two invoice groups total 650.00 and 220.00.
cases.derivation: B01 is not overdue at one hour against four-hour grace. B02's overlap is not resolved by row order. B03 has zero detention and 7.00 fuel; a -7.00 undercharge exceeds 2.14 tolerance. Only B03/B04 contribute to the computed variance.

cases.design: An invoice line has amount 12oops rather than a money string.
cases.derivation: The amount is outside the declared numeric schema; bundle validation must finish with rejection before computing business artifacts.

cases.design: LG-C01 has two highest eligible POD revisions with different delivered-unit evidence; its billed amount is 550.00. LG-C02 has unambiguous matching evidence for 110.00.
cases.derivation: No revision or row-order tie-break can establish C01's delivery evidence. Its entire amount is quarantined; C02 remains independently computable.

candidates.title: Maintenance readiness and resource-window conflict plan
candidates.trigger: Weekly snapshot of fictional work packages, reserved kits, resources, candidate windows, commitments and prerequisites.
candidates.start: Freeze planning horizon, snapshot cutoff and grid, then validate all administrative planning exports.
candidates.end: Produce contingent proposed resource slots, readiness/backlog, observed conflict explanations and resource load totals for a human planner.
candidates.boundary: Not safe-to-work clearance. No physical equipment operations, isolation/lockout instructions, permits, authorization decisions, actual scheduling, dispatch or business-system writes.

fields.prerequisite_id: id external to current work orders
fields.completed_at: instant when complete, null when open

joins: Requirements and kits -> work_order_id + item_id; kits are reserved to that order, not reusable shared stock.
Crew candidates -> craft_code and kind crew; area and optional tool -> fixed resource IDs.
Windows and commitments -> resource_id; all required resources must fit simultaneously.
Predecessor -> internal work_order_id or explicit external prerequisite-status row; missing or unresolved evidence is not completion.

rules.description: Review work order resource/material requirements as planning context, without performing maintenance.
Compare required resources and start/end needs with resource availability; keep actual authorization outside the scenario.
Administrative approval, sufficient order-reserved kits, and explicit predecessor evidence are necessary for a proposal; future kit availability changes its lower bound.
Reject dependency cycles. Recompute the dependency-resolved set after each decision and select by priority, due time, ID; deferred predecessors defer successors.
Greedy increasing grid starts, then lexicographic crew ID; one crew plus fixed area/optional tool, each capacity one, for the full duration.
Use UTC half-open intervals, horizon-relative grid, full containment in a single window per resource, and end <= due/horizon end. Do not stitch adjacent staffing windows.
Record actual rejected candidate reasons and conflicting IDs; exhausted search yields an explicit deferred order, not an invented slot.
Every work order is proposed or deferred; resource load separates proposed and committed minutes; no result implies clearance or real scheduling.

steps.trace: Actual order/resource counts and planning limits.

steps.procedure: Check schemas, quantities, times and dependency graph; reject malformed records/cycles.
steps.trace: Concrete validation facts or cycle member IDs.

steps.procedure: Evaluate gates and contingent earliest bounds in dependency-aware priority order.
steps.trace: Actual gate results, shortages, predecessor and kit bounds.

steps.procedure: Iterate actual grid slots and eligible crews against windows and bookings.
steps.trace: Observed tested/selected slots, crew choices and allocation IDs.

steps.procedure: Explain rejected candidates and unresolved work without changing commitments.
steps.trace: Real conflicting resource/order IDs and deferred reasons.

steps.procedure: Aggregate proposed and committed resource minutes separately.
steps.trace: Actual crew/tool/area allocation totals.

steps.procedure: Emit proposals, readiness, deferred actions and no-authorization warning.
steps.trace: Final proposal/deferred counts, durations and final artifact facts.

output_design: Readiness matrix with administrative, kit and prerequisite findings per work order.
Contingent proposals with start/end, crew, fixed resources and predecessor dependencies.
Observed search/conflict summary with conflicting commitments and proposals.
Deferred work queue with evidence or rescheduling action for human planning.
Resource proposed/committed minutes and complete order accounting.

numeric_semantics.time: Explicit offsets normalized to UTC; whole seconds; grid relative to horizon start.
numeric_semantics.crew_choice: earliest feasible grid start first, then lexicographic crew ID
numeric_semantics.work_choice: dependency-resolved set recomputed after each decision; priority then due time then work_order_id
numeric_semantics.duration_constraint: Full duration lies in one window for each resource; proposed end <= due time and horizon end.
numeric_semantics.load: Sum integer proposed minutes per required resource; existing committed minutes reported separately.
numeric_semantics.optimization_claim: Deterministic greedy heuristic only; not globally optimal and not Maximo's algorithm.

cases.design: Six work orders priority D01-D06. CE1 available 08-16, CM1 08-12, T1 08-16. Existing CE1 commitment 09-10 and T1 commitment 11-12. Areas A1 08-12, A2 09-15, A3 08-12, A4 08-16. D04 requires 3 kit units but has 1; D05 has an open external predecessor.
cases.derivation: D01 ends exactly at CE1's commitment start. D02's 09:00 through 11:30 candidate starts collide with CE1 or T1, so 12:00 is first feasible. D03 follows proposed D01; D06 fits after D03. D04/D05 fail readiness before slot allocation.

cases.design: Four new orders, two electrical crews, full-horizon A/B/tool windows. CE-A01 committed 13-14Z, tool T-A1 committed 15-16Z. A01 is 90 minutes A/tool, A02 60 minutes B/tool, A03 30 minutes A/no tool after A01, A04 60 minutes B/no tool with reserved kit available 17:30Z. All due 18Z.
cases.derivation: Earliest slot takes CE-A02 for A01 rather than waiting for lexicographically first CE-A01. A02 cannot fit across tool's 15-16 booking and starts at 16. A03 starts at predecessor finish with no tool requirement. A04's ready-at bound leaves only 30 minutes for a 60-minute job.

cases.design: Five new orders, E-B1 and M-B1 whole-horizon crews/tool, X window 08-10 and Y 09-12. Priority-1 B02 depends on priority-2 B01. B03 needs an impossible 60-minute X/tool interval after 09 and by 10; B04 needs Y/no tool after 09:45; B05 lacks planning approval.
cases.derivation: Recomputing the dependency-resolved priority set lets B02 run immediately after B01, before B03. Half-open adjacency permits B02 at 09:00 and B04 at 09:45. B03 cannot fit a full hour before X closes at 10.

cases.design: A work order has boolean true as duration_minutes.
cases.derivation: JSON true is not a positive integer duration, even though Python bool subclasses int.

cases.design: Two valid work orders each declare the other as an internal prerequisite.
cases.derivation: Neither order can precede the other consistently; graph validation rejects the bundle without inventing completion or authorization.

specific_tests: crew lexicographic tie and earlier-slot precedence

candidates.title: Approved time and expense to client billing draft reconciliation
candidates.trigger: Billing-cutoff exports for multiple fictional projects with time, expenses, approval histories, prior billing and draft details.
candidates.start: Freeze service period and cutoff, then inventory nine independent logical exports.
candidates.end: Produce eligible candidate amounts, draft differences, project cap summaries and owned correction/clarification holds.
candidates.boundary: No approval or recall action, reimbursement, real invoice creation/send, proforma confirmation, AR/GL posting, customer contact, tax or FX decisions.
joins: Time/expense -> project_id for client, currency, cap and owner.
Time -> project_id + role_code + project currency + service date in [valid_from, valid_to), exactly one rate.
Expense -> category + currency for explicit policy; expense currency must equal project currency.
Approval/billed/draft line -> entry_type + entry_id; current entry project/currency must agree with identity evidence.
Draft detail -> draft_id -> project, currency and service period.
Historical posted entries absent from current intake still count toward the project cap when service_date is in period and billed_at <= cutoff.

rules.description: Approval and recall status matter to billing evidence, but the baseline does not perform any approval or financial transition.
Review draft transaction details before customer invoicing; stop before confirmation and actuals creation.
Quarantine identity/approval contradictions; otherwise check service period, chargeability, prior billing, latest as-of approval, then pricing/expense policy.
Use unique effective project/role/currency rate; round minutes * hourly_rate / 60 per entry before summing.
Per-entry category/currency cap and receipt threshold are explicit. Require receipt at or above threshold; exceeding cap or currency mismatch holds the whole expense, without truncation or FX.
Zero-tolerance add/update/remove diagnostics; duplicate entry details or multiple active drafts for a project/period require clarification, not arbitrary selection.
Prior billed-in-period plus eligible new exceeding cap holds the whole project's new amount; equality is allowed. No partial allocation or inferred credit.
Account for all entries/drafts/projects; preserve per-currency totals and partial-comparison boundaries; produce local review recommendations only.

steps.procedure: Inventory nine exports, service period and cutoff.
steps.trace: Actual project/time/expense/draft counts and cutoff facts.

steps.procedure: Check schemas, IDs, minutes, amounts, currencies, date ranges and approval enums.
steps.trace: Validated record counts or exact offending field.

steps.procedure: Join projects, entries, approval histories, rates/policies, ledger and draft details.
steps.trace: Selected entry IDs with matching approval/rate/draft evidence.

steps.procedure: Choose unique eligible approval revision and explicit exclusion/hold dispositions.
steps.trace: Actual approved/pending/recalled, billed and period decisions.

steps.procedure: Calculate time per entry and enforce expense receipt/cap/currency policy.
steps.trace: Actual minutes/rate/amount, expense limits and eligibility branches.

steps.procedure: Find missing, differing, duplicate and ineligible draft details without modifying them.
steps.trace: Real expected/draft amounts and proposed diagnostic actions.

steps.procedure: Add prior period billing and eligible new charges, then apply whole-project holds.
steps.trace: Prior/new/cap/overage values by project and currency.

steps.procedure: Assign correction and clarification items; suppress speculative changes for ambiguous evidence.
steps.trace: Actual issue owners, affected entries/projects and amounts.

steps.procedure: Emit complete local draft reconciliation, project summaries and review-only actions.
steps.trace: Final eligible/held/excluded facts with separate currency totals.

output_design: Entry eligibility and charge table with approval/rate/policy provenance and excluded/held reasons.
Draft comparison details with missing/update/remove/clarify diagnostics and original line identities.
Project cap consumption including prior billing and whole-project hold amount.
Owned correction/clarification packet and per-currency complete/partial totals.

numeric_semantics.approval: unique highest revision recorded_at <= as_of; future ignored, conflicting highest held
numeric_semantics.cap: hold project only when prior_billed + eligible_new > period_cap
numeric_semantics.currency: No FX or mixed-currency grand total
numeric_semantics.partial_billing: Out of scope; a posted current entry is wholly excluded, never implicitly split.
output_order: draft differences by draft_id then entry_type then entry_id then line_id

cases.design: Two USD projects. P1 cap 2000/hourly rate 100; P2 cap 500/rate 120. Travel cap 100, meals cap 50, receipt threshold 50. Six time entries, four expenses, two drafts, prior billing and multiple approval states.

independent_expectations.p2_diagnostic_only: Missing T5 at 60.00; project remains held.

cases.derivation: P1: 120/60*100 + 90/60*100 + 80 = 430. Its draft 560 becomes 430 by -10-100-100+80. P2: 120/60*120 + 30/60*120 +40=340; 200+340=540 exceeds cap by 40, so all 340 is held. E2/E3 are not truncated or reimbursed.

cases.design: One new project with 1000 cap; rate 150 through October 14 and 180 from October 15; four time entries and three expenses. Changed travel/meals caps 150/60, receipt threshold 50. Recalled revision before cutoff and future reapproval after cutoff; one nonchargeable entry.
cases.derivation: 50/60*150=125; 75/60*180=225; 125+225+49.99+40=439.99. Adding prior 560.01 reaches, but does not exceed, 1000. A3's future reapproval is ineligible; remove its 60 from 499.99. EA2 hits the receipt threshold exactly.

cases.design: New USD and EUR projects, changed receipt threshold 30, per-entry fractional-cent rounding, currency mismatch, exact cap, missing draft line and service-period end exclusion.

held_expenses.EB2: EUR 15.00 against USD project, no conversion

cases.derivation: Each 1/60*100 line rounds to 1.67, hence 3.34 rather than aggregated 3.33; adding 20 yields 23.34. Draft 21.66 needs +0.01+1.67. EUR prior 160 plus new 90 equals 250 cap. No cross-currency sum is meaningful.

cases.design: An expense has amount -12.00, outside the positive-charge-only money schema.
cases.derivation: Negative amounts are not interpreted as implicit credits or reimbursements; reject the bundle before financial calculations.

cases.design: C1 has two highest approval revisions, approved and recalled, for a 60-minute 100/hour entry shown on a 100.00 draft. Separate-project C2 has valid approved 30 minutes at 120/hour and a matching 60.00 draft.
cases.derivation: The conflicting top revisions cannot establish approval or recall, so C1 has no computed candidate and no speculative removal. C2 independently computes 30/60*120=60 and matches its draft.

specific_tests: receipt and expense cap exact boundaries
service and effective rate interval boundaries
duplicate drafts/details and conflicting approval evidence
ambiguous evidence never becomes an automatic removal or posting
